question.text: An Indian PM investing in US Treasuries for her INR-denominated client faces which UNIQUE risk compared to domestic G-Sec investing?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that investment in a non-domestic currency always carries currency conversion risk, because adverse exchange-rate movements can wipe out returns from global fixed-income investments. For an Indian INR-denominated client, USD/INR currency risk is the unique additional exposure not present in domestic G-Sec investing. The Trap: Credit, liquidity, and duration risks all exist in domestic bond portfolios too; they are not the distinguishing risk of investing offshore. Currency swaps are noted as a tool to protect against this risk for international non-domestic-currency investments. Note: Page 348 covers legal and currency risk for global fixed income; page 349 supports currency swaps as a hedging tool.
